# aibris v0.12.3

This patch release fixes a data-loss bug in `aibris clean --strip`. Upgrade
if you use `--strip`.

## Highlights

- **`clean --strip` no longer removes files outside the worktree** (#569).
  When a worktree's `android/` or `ios/` directory was a symlink to another
  directory, the scan inventoried `android/build` (or `ios/build`) through the
  symlink and strip deleted that directory outside the checkout. A stale or
  edited inventory entry could also strip a sibling worktree's subtree or a
  git-ignored directory that is not a regenerable position. Strip now
  re-authorizes every subtree right before removal: it must be a clean path
  strictly inside the unit, still produced by the inventory rules, free of
  symlinks between the unit and itself, and the same directory that passed the
  Git checks. Removal runs through an `os.Root` opened on the unit, and the
  scan inventory no longer follows symlinks.
- **Windows worktree path identity** stays consistent between discovery and
  blocked-alias keys (#564).
- **Development**: faster and less flaky tests, a `make check` static gate
  (gofmt, `go mod tidy -diff`, vet, staticcheck, govulncheck, shellcheck) run
  in CI, and additional edge-case coverage (#565, #566, #567, #570).

## Compatibility impact

- [x] **No compatibility change.** Documented CLI flags, JSON fields,
  defaults, and exit behavior are unchanged.

`--strip` may now keep a subtree it previously removed and report why (for
example `symlink on the path to the subtree` or `unit changed since scan`).
Skipped subtrees were already part of the strip outcome.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or (Unix):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.12.3
# or (Windows PowerShell):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Safety

- Strip never removes a worktree unit, and now never removes anything outside
  the unit or anything other than an inventoried regenerable subtree.
- A symlink swapped to another directory *inside the same unit* in the instant
  between the final check and removal remains an accepted residual risk; it
  requires a concurrent process racing the cleanup.
- All v0.12.2 guarantees are unchanged: `plain-dir` and mixed-marker owners
  stay review-only; active worktrees, live agent state, and the current
  working directory are protected; `--apfs-snapshots` stays opt-in; default
  `clean --json` output stays path-redacted.

## Windows status

Unchanged from v0.12.2: Windows native support is installable and
reproducible (`install.ps1`, case-insensitive path canonicalization, and the
`windows-safety` CI job). Real vendor agent worktree layouts on Windows,
end-to-end delete mutation, and native arm64 execution remain experimental and
unmeasured. See `docs/WINDOWS.md`.
